summary: A compact shortcut to one destination.

useWhen.text: A compact shortcut to one destination.

from.quote: A compact shortcut to one destination.

useWhen.text: Offer a small set of quick actions: a group of tiles, each a shortcut to one destination.

from.quote: Offer a small set of quick actions

avoidWhen.text: Explaining a destination in a sentence: explanatory sentences turn a shortcut into a card. A tile holds one short label.

from.quote: explanatory sentences that turn a shortcut into a card

anatomy.holds: The icon slot, an IconCapsule by default: reinforces the destination and receives the tile's full mode object.

from.quote: Reinforces the destination and receives the owner’s full mode object.

anatomy.holds: label: names one destination with a short, familiar term.

from.quote: Names one destination with a short, familiar term.

anatomy.holds: The fixed 168 × 90 surface and its token-driven styling, owned by ActionTile.

from.quote: ActionTile owns the fixed 168 × 90 surface and token-driven styling.

placementAdvice.text: Group tiles in an HStack: the HStack owns the responsive group while each fixed tile keeps one destination.

from.quote: A public HStack owns the responsive group while each fixed tile keeps one destination.

placementAdvice.text: Let the surrounding layout wrap or scroll around the tiles.

from.quote: Let the surrounding public layout wrap or scroll

placementAdvice.text: In a wide host, the tile keeps its intrinsic footprint inside the available space.

from.quote: The tile keeps its intrinsic footprint inside available space.

placementAdvice.text: In a narrow host, the host adapts around the tile; the tile itself stays 168 × 90.

from.quote: The host adapts around the tile; the tile itself stays 168 × 90.

configuration.text: Keep the label and the icon focused on the same destination.

from.quote: Keep both focused on the same destination.

configuration.text: Use an icon that matches the destination, such as a card icon for a card destination.

from.quote: Use a card icon for a card destination.

configuration.text: Change both the label and its icon together.

from.quote: Change both the label and its icon together.

configuration.text: Do not pair a label with another destination's icon, such as a cards icon on Savings: it makes the shortcut ambiguous.

from.quote: A cards icon makes the Savings shortcut ambiguous.

configuration.text: Keep the destination distinct from neighboring shortcuts.

from.quote: Keep the destination distinct from neighboring shortcuts.

configuration.text: icon expects an IconCapsule or a compatible component; when it is a React element, ActionTile passes its modes to it.
The icon capsule inherits the modes supplied to ActionTile.

from.quote: The icon capsule inherits the owner modes supplied to ActionTile.

configuration.text: Supplying onPress makes the tile actionable.

from.quote: Supplying onPress makes the tile actionable.

configuration.text: Do not invent disabled or loading states: the public API does not expose them.

from.quote: The public API does not expose disabled or loading states, so do not invent them.

configuration.text: ActionTile owns a fixed width and height (168 × 90); do not resize the tile with style patches.

from.quote: do not resize the tile with style patches.

rules.text: One icon, one short label, one destination.

from.quote: One icon. One short label. One destination.

rules.text: Short nouns usually work best for the label.

from.quote: Short nouns usually work best.

rules.text: The icon and the short label should describe the same place.

from.quote: The icon and short label should describe the same place.

rules.text: Use compact labels: Cards, Savings and Payments are easy to scan in a group.

from.quote: Cards, Savings, and Payments are easy to scan in a group.

rules.text: Give each visible tile a destination name that distinguishes it from its siblings.

from.quote: Each visible tile needs a destination name that distinguishes it from its siblings.

rules.text: Do not repeat a vague label such as More on several tiles: duplicate More tiles do not reveal where either shortcut leads.

from.quote: Duplicate More tiles do not reveal where either shortcut leads.

rules.text: Do not turn the label into a sentence such as “Open the place where you manage all your cards”: long instructions overwhelm a compact shortcut.

from.quote: Long instructions overwhelm a compact shortcut.

bad: Open the place where you manage all your cards

states.when: Without onPress: display only; the tile presents the shortcut information without activation.

from.quote: Without onPress the tile presents the shortcut information without activation.

states.when: With onPress the whole tile activates the named destination.

from.quote: With onPress the whole tile activates the named destination.

from.quote: Use distinct destination names

doDont.dont: Turn the label into a sentence
doDont.why: Long instructions overwhelm a compact shortcut.

from.quote: Keep the label short

doDont.dont: Pair the label with another destination
doDont.why: A cards icon makes the Savings shortcut ambiguous.

from.quote: Match icon and destination

examples.purpose: Quick actions, the guide's In context: an HStack wraps three actionable tiles, each with its own label and matching IconCapsule icon, each opening one destination.
examples.jsx:
<HStack wrap>
  <ActionTile
    label="Cards"
    icon={<IconCapsule iconName="ic_cards" />}
    onPress={() => {}}
  />
  <ActionTile
    label="Savings"
    icon={<IconCapsule iconName="ic_savings" />}
    onPress={() => {}}
  />
  <ActionTile
    label="Payments"
    icon={<IconCapsule iconName="ic_payments" />}
    onPress={() => {}}
  />
</HStack>

from.quote: A public HStack owns the responsive group while each fixed tile keeps one destination.

examples.purpose: A static, display-only tile: without onPress it presents the shortcut information without activation.

from.quote: Without onPress the tile presents the shortcut information without activation.

examples.purpose: A Savings tile: the label and its icon change together, so the savings icon reinforces the Savings label.

from.quote: Change both the label and its icon together.

props.description: Label text, e.g. "Cards". Default "Cards", from the component source.

props.name: icon
props.description: Icon component slot. Expects an IconCapsule or compatible component. Modes will be passed to this slot if it's a valid React element.

gaps.text: ActionTile has no disabled or loading state: its public API offers only an optional action (onPress).

Figma's live Action Tile icon capsule resolves AppearanceBrand Neutral with Emphasis High, while the supplied Storybook reference selects Primary appearance with Medium emphasis; the guide follows the Storybook reference.
